name: agent_chunk_step_offsets_play_out
description: Pins the playout clock for GateServerMessage.intervention_chunk: a chunk's steps are due at RECEIVE TIME PLUS each step's own t_offset_ns — the chunk is a trajectory over time, not a burst to be drained on the next tick. One chunk carries two steps 100 ms apart, addressed to different parts so each substitute names which step actuated: the tick at arrival substitutes the tOffsetNs 0 step ('left'), the tick 50 ms later holds because the second step is not due yet, and the tick at the offset substitutes it ('right'). A sender's own emit clock (t_emitted_ns) is deliberately NOT the anchor — a remote sender's clock is not an anchor on this side — and the timings DISCRIMINATE the two readings rather than merely asserting one: the chunk declares tEmittedNs 100 ms before it arrives (the transit and clock skew a remote sender's stamp carries), so an emit-anchored implementation would make the second step due at the middle tick, which this scenario requires to hold. Read the three ticks as the discriminator they are: at arrival both readings substitute 'left'; 50 ms later receive-anchoring holds while emit-anchoring would substitute 'right'; at the offset receive-anchoring substitutes 'right'. Judgment calls: HOLD_FIRST so no blend window is open; the claim is ACTOR_KIND_AGENT because this arm is the one a hosted agent streams on; part names and the 7-value part width come from the bimanual fixture.
